Is this a private tour?
faq.answer: Yes. Only you and the people you book with travel in the vehicle, with your own driver for the four days. You choose the start date, the pick-up time and how long you stay at each stop. There is no minimum group size, and the tour runs every day of the year.

faq.question: What is the desert camp like?
faq.answer: The camp sits among the dunes of Erg Chebbi, about an hour by camel from Merzouga. Tents have proper beds, blankets and lighting, and dinner is served in a main tent or outside under the stars. Depending on the level you book, tents share a bathroom block or have their own toilet and shower. There is usually electricity for charging phones in the evening.

faq.question: Can I skip the camel ride?
faq.answer: Yes. If you prefer not to ride, or if someone in your group has back or mobility problems, you can reach the camp by 4x4 instead, and still walk up a dune for sunset. Camels are led on foot by experienced handlers and walk slowly, so most travellers, including children from about 5 or 6 years old, find the ride easy.

faq.question: When is the best time for this desert tour?
faq.answer: Spring (March to May) and autumn (September to November) are the most comfortable, with warm days and mild nights in the desert. Winter days are sunny but desert nights can drop close to 0 °C, and snow sometimes closes the Tichka pass for a few hours. In summer, temperatures in Merzouga often pass 40 °C; the itinerary keeps the camel ride for the late afternoon, and many hotels have pools.

faq.question: How much cash should I bring?
faq.answer: Lunches, drinks, entrance fees and tips are paid on the way, mostly in cash, and cards are rarely accepted in the desert. As a guide, plan around 150–250 dirhams per person per day for lunch and drinks, a little extra for the Ait Ben Haddou guide or film studios if you want them, and tips for the camel handlers and your driver. Withdraw dirhams in Marrakech before leaving.
